svg.text: How the synthetic concurrent disorders dataset was curated
Survey-weighted NSDUH 2024 estimates of co-occurring mental illness and substance use disorder → calibrated Synthea 3.3.0 module → validated, OMOP-ready CSV
National Survey on Drug Use and Health
MH = AMIPY (any mental illness, past year)
(all U.S. adults; four cells sum to 100%)
Per synthetic patient, the module concurrent_disorders.json (177 states) runs these steps:
SNOMED CT: MDD 370143000 · Anxiety disorder 197480006 · Alcohol 15167005
Built-in Synthea modules overridden to protect the calibration
Replaced (3): depression, anxiety & substance-use screeners — scores now
follow the patient's profile and never create diagnoses
* Survey categories are not diagnoses: the MH-category → diagnosis mapping, treatment content and all timing are documented simulation assumptions (NSDUH is cross-sectional).
Massachusetts demography · ages 18–85 · alive at end
CSV export = input format of OHDSI ETL-Synthea (v3.3.0)
run_manifest.json: SHA-256 of jar, NSDUH file, modules
Group distribution: NSDUH target vs synthetic (n = 10,000)
Target = NSDUH stratum probabilities applied to the synthetic age/sex mix; whiskers = exact 95% CI
37 / 40 age × sex × group cells: target in 95% CI
100% of MH/SUD diagnoses dated inside window
0 uncalibrated MH/SUD codes from other modules
MH only 14.3% vs 15.2%; MDD share ≈ 2 pts low (sampling)
Not yet run: CSV → PostgreSQL database synthetic_concurrent (schemas synthea, cdm, results)
OHDSI ETLSyntheaBuilder → OMOP CDM 5.4 with Athena vocabularies (SNOMED, RxNorm, LOINC) → Data Quality Dashboard → cohort checks vs person_ground_truth.csv
Synthetic data for software testing, cohort development, teaching and preliminary methods work — not for estimating treatment effects. NSDUH excludes institutionalized populations.
